step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates Banque Pictet's AWS multi-account governance and secure network topology. The diagram is divided into External accounts (EXT), Internal accounts (INT), Corporate Data Center (DC), and centralized governance/security services. Data ingestion flows unidirectionally from the Internet Gateway in EXT accounts through AWS managed services (S3/SQS/SNS) into VPC Endpoints in INT accounts to prevent data exfiltration. Internal VPCs connect via Transit Gateway and VPN to the on-premises corporate Router. Centralized governance uses AWS Organizations to enforce SCPs and deploy AWS Config rules. Security findings from AWS Config and GuardDuty are aggregated into Security Hub for threat visibility and alerting.

graph.name: Banque Pictet AWS Multi-Account Network and Governance Architecture
graph.notes: Architecture features multi-account isolation (EXT vs INT), controlled unidirectional ingestion via S3/SQS/SNS, hybrid connectivity via Transit Gateway and VPN, centralized policy enforcement via SCPs and Config, and consolidated security monitoring via Security Hub.

nodes.name: INTERNET GW
nodes.notes: Located in external accounts (EXT) to manage inbound/outbound internet traffic.

nodes.name: S3 / SQS / SNS
nodes.notes: AWS managed services enabling controlled, unidirectional data acquisition from internet-facing accounts to internal accounts.

nodes.name: VPC ENDPOINTS
nodes.notes: Located in internal accounts (INT) to consume data securely from AWS managed services.

nodes.name: TRANSIT GW
nodes.notes: Central network hub interconnecting internal account VPCs and hybrid connections.

nodes.name: VPN
nodes.notes: Encrypted VPN connection linking Transit Gateway to the corporate data center.

nodes.name: ROUTER
nodes.notes: Corporate network router in the on-premises data center.

nodes.name: ORGANIZATIONS
nodes.notes: AWS Organizations managing multi-account hierarchy and central policy deployment.

nodes.name: SCPs
nodes.notes: Service Control Policies restricting regions, services, and security guardrails across accounts.

nodes.name: CONFIG
nodes.notes: AWS Config rules deployed centrally across all accounts to enforce compliance (e.g., requiring Lambda inside VPC).

nodes.name: GUARDDUTY
nodes.notes: Threat detection service monitoring AWS account activity and network behavior.

nodes.name: SECURITY HUB
nodes.notes: Central security findings aggregator collecting compliance alerts and anomalies for response.

edges.notes: Internet traffic is received by external accounts and passed into managed services.
Unidirectional data transfer from S3/SQS/SNS into VPC Endpoints within internal accounts.
Internal VPC traffic routes through Transit Gateway.
Transit Gateway routes traffic through the IPsec VPN connection.
VPN tunnel connects to the corporate router in the on-premises data center.
AWS Organizations manages and applies SCP policies across organization units.
AWS Organizations deploys AWS Config compliance rules across all member accounts.
Config forwards rule compliance assessments to Security Hub.
GuardDuty forwards threat detections to Security Hub.
